elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Article XXII, which gave Licensor a right to be notified of any bona fide third-party asset-purchase or change-of-control offer and to take that transaction on the same terms (a disclosure/right-to-match, i.e. most-favoured-offer, mechanic running in Vendor's favour), is rendered as 'ARTICLE XXII [INTENTIONALLY OMITTED]'. The defined 'Right of First Refusal' and 'Exercise Period' obligations no longer appear in operative language, and no other cited fee or payment article imposes a best-price/best-terms undertaking on Licensee.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: its stated condition does not apply because, after the redline, no Customer MFN/right-to-match obligation survives at all (Article XXII is struck in full), so there is no scope to confine to a defined product.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no Customer MFN remains after deletion of Article XXII, so the former 'During the term of this Agreement' duration is eliminated rather than shortened; the durational cap has nothing to bite on.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: with the entire right-to-match mechanic (five-business-day Exercise Period and matching right) removed, there is no comparison obligation requiring like-for-like carve-outs.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the only MFN-family obligation burdening Licensee (the Article XXII disclosure plus right-to-match on a third-party asset sale or change of control) is struck outright, and no Vendor-granted MFN existed that could be lost.

Minimality is satisfied on the edit itself: only Article XXII's operative mechanic and the conforming lead-in ('In the event the Licensor declines or fails to exercise in full the Right of First Refusal before the expiration of the Exercise Period,') are removed, no survival tails, procedures or extra requirements are added, and the Customer-favourable closing sentence is retained rather than deleted.

Intent defect — internally inconsistent rendered output: the heading reads 'ARTICLE XXII [INTENTIONALLY OMITTED]' yet operative text ('The Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party.') still follows under it. An article declared intentionally omitted cannot carry a surviving covenant. Repair: either delete the residual sentence with the rest of the article, or move it out from under the omitted heading and restate it as a self-standing provision.

Intent defect — dangling reference: the retained sentence refers to 'the transaction with the third party' when the deleted text was the only place a third-party offer, asset purchase or merger was described. Repair in operative language, e.g.: 'ARTICLE XXII TRANSFERS. Licensee may sell all or substantially all of its assets, or engage in any merger or consolidation, with any third party without notice to, or any right of first refusal, matching right or consent of, Licensor.'

Confirm no other article cross-references 'Article XXII', the 'Right of First Refusal' or the 'Exercise Period' (e.g. an assignment, change-of-control or notices provision); the cited extract does not show the rest of the document, and any surviving cross-reference would become orphaned by this deletion.
